I am an Assistant Professor of Management in the Department of Management at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, where I am also a Seacrest Teaching Fellow. I earned my B.S.B.A., M.B.A., and Ph.D. in Business (Management) from UNL, completing the Ph.D. in 2021 under Larry J. Williams and Troy A. Smith.

My research sits at the intersection of **leadership** and **research methodology**. On the substantive side, I study how informal leadership emerges in groups and teams, and how employees experience belonging to multiple teams at once. On the methodological side, I work on latent variable modeling, including factor analysis, item parceling, and the modeling of multidimensional constructs.

I am active in the Academy of Management's Research Methods Division, where I serve as the 2026 AOM-CARMA Consortium Chair, and I serve on the Board of Directors of the Southern Management Association. I also teach entrepreneurship, organizational behavior, and design thinking, and I research how AI can be integrated into teaching.

## Research interests

- Informal and emergent leadership
- Multiple team membership
- Structural equation modeling and latent variable methodology
- Multidimensional constructs, parceling, and model fit

## Recent highlights

- **2026:** Received the AOM Network of Leadership Scholars Early Career Rising Star Award.
- **2026:** Named Journal of Organizational Behavior's 2025 Reviewer of the Year.
- **2026:** *Methods and theory for using parcels in management research* (with L. J. Williams and T. A. Smith) published in the *Journal of Management*.
- **Upcoming:** Southern Management Association meeting (October 2026) and an invited talk for the AOM Community Accelerator Program in Riga, Latvia (April 2027).
